summary.circularity_avoided: the target is KrSEQ's repeat range; no feature uses KrSEQ's own spread, only the other measures of the same exam set
summary.control: the base rate. Always answering reliable is correct in 257 of 300 eyes, so accuracy is not a usable score; the question is whether a flagged subgroup carries a materially higher rate
summary.scope: a different instrument and cohort from the 89 surgical eyes; this establishes whether unreliability is PREDICTABLE at all, not a flag for those patients

single_exam_features.note: Features from one exam only, no repeats: zone mean, power mean, the 3 mm minus 6 mm difference and the absolute zone difference. Lift over the base rate ranges 0.65 to 1.30, i.e. at or near chance; the absolute zone difference is below chance at 0.65.
single_exam_features.conclusion: The flag is not available from a single exam. It requires repeated measurement of the same eye, after which the spread in one channel predicts instability in another.
single_exam_features.limitation: Because it needs repeats, it cannot separate an unstable eye from an unstable measurement session. Both are detectable, neither is distinguished.
